key_insight: A surrogate-assisted inverse-design workflow can rapidly optimize an all-oxide thermophotovoltaic emitter to achieve a high, narrowband emission peak aligned for efficient TPV operation.
engineering_relevance: Using ITO/Al2O3 on sapphire offers a more thermally robust emitter platform than metal-dielectric designs, which is important for high-temperature TPV systems.
method: Trained ExtraTrees surrogate models on FDTD-generated spectra from systematically varied thickness and period parameters.
Used Bayesian optimization with a penalty-augmented objective to enforce E_peak > 0.90 while minimizing FWHM and maximizing in-band emission fraction.
Validated the optimized geometry with full FDTD simulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation via narrowband-emission metrics including E_peak, peak wavelength, FWHM, and in-band fraction, with the optimized structure confirmed by FDTD.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the surrogate training data, so optimization may be less reliable outside the sampled design space.
paper_title: Surrogate-Assisted Inverse Design and Temperature-Dependent Electrothermal Analysis of an All-Oxide Narrowband Thermophotovoltaic Emitter
